messages:
sophie (Support): Heads-up — Escalation from Acme Ops. They saw a ~5x token bill spike yesterday after upgrading to our python sdk v1.12. Customer says retries kept firing even when upstream returned 429 with Retry-After. Logs attached.

acme_ops (Customer): Repro steps:
````python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=..., retry_policy=None)  # default in v1.12
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=512)
````
We sent a burst of 100 concurrent requests. A few got 429s with `Retry-After: 10`. Our app observed immediate retry attempts (0s, 0.5s, 1s...), leading to more 429s and billing. Trace: `redwood._client.RetryError: too many attempts` and lots of repeated request ids in the logs.

sophie (Support): Thanks — any SDK change notes that could explain this? Customer pinned to v1.11.4 and the problem disappears. They want guidance on whether to pin or patch.

alex (Eng): Hmm. v1.12 did change retry behavior. We removed the default jitter and changed default backoff schedule to a fixed linear ramp for latency predictability. That was intended to reduce tail latency, but I didn't realize it would ignore `Retry-After` semantics in some code paths. Can you paste the header handling?

acme_ops (Customer): Header we saw: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`Retry-After: 10`
But SDK kept sending at ~0.5s intervals. Sample log snippet: `Request id=cl-abc123 status=429 retry_in=0.5 attempt=2` repeated.

maria (SDK): Confirmed root cause: we renamed `respect_retry_after` -> `honor_retry_after` in the config and the mapping at Client init had a bug so the default ended up false in the shipped wheel. Also we changed the backoff function to `linear_backoff` without jitter. Combined, for servers that expect clients to wait for `Retry-After`, clients retried aggressively. Apologies.

maria (SDK): Immediate remediation options:
- Recommend customers pin to `redwood-sdk==1.11.4` to restore previous behavior: `pip install redwood-sdk==1.11.4`
- Short-term patch for v1.12: set explicit retry config on Client: `Client(retry_policy={"honor_retry_after": True, "backoff": "exponential", "max_attempts": 4})`
- We will cut a 1.12.1 patch to flip default back to honoring `Retry-After` and restore jitter.

sophie (Support): Can you provide the exact pip command and a one-liner we can give the customer for rollback? Also any billing mitigation notes?

maria (SDK): Rollback pip one-liner: `pip install 'redwood-sdk==1.11.4' --force-reinstall`
Billing mitigation: set a short-term per-key rate limit in Console (or create a quota rule) and request billing team for a goodwill credit if the spike is large. Also advise to set `max_attempts` low and enable `honor_retry_after`.

alex (Eng): I've opened GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/827 (internal) and a PR for fix is #829. Will prioritize 1.12.1 today.

support-bot: Deploy bot: patch release process started for `redwood-sdk` v1.12.1 — build queued.

acme_ops (Customer): Thank you — we'll pin for now and enable `honor_retry_after` in our config. Please keep us posted.

maria (SDK): Action items for SDK: revert default mapping bug, restore jitter, add integration test for honoring `Retry-After`, and publish release notes with clear guidance about pinning. Also add a migration note in docs: "v1.12 changed retry defaults; pin to 1.11.x if you need previous behavior."

sophie (Support): Marking this escalated to SDK team. I'll follow up with billing and the customer. :thumbsup:
